# Welcome {.unnumbered}

::: {.hero}
## One source, trustworthy results, many outputs

In this workshop you will build a small research manuscript in which the prose,
analysis, figures, tables, and references live together. You will render it to
HTML and PDF.
:::

## By the end

You will be able to:

- explain literate programming in practical terms;
- write structured prose in Markdown;
- combine R code and narrative in a `.qmd` file;
- use relative paths, citations, figures, tables, and cross-references;
- render one source document to HTML and PDF
- start your PhD thesis using the [quarto template](https://github.com/quarto-monash/thesis)

## What you will make

The workshop project contains a short manuscript analysing a synthetic training study.

The data are synthetic, small, and stored inside the project. No network
connection, account, or API key is required during the activities.

::: {.callout-important}
## Download before the workshop

- [Participant starter project](materials/downloads/quarto-workshop-starter.zip)
- [Completed project](materials/downloads/quarto-workshop-complete.zip)

Work from the starter project. Keep the completed project closed unless you need
to recover from a missed step or want to compare your result at the end.
:::

## Illustrative running order

The detailed chapters are also designed to work as a reference after the
workshop. They contain more examples than need to be demonstrated live, so the
facilitator can select material and adjust the timings for the group.

| Time | Topic | Product |
|---|---|---|
| 00:00–00:15 | Setup checkpoint | First successful render |
| 00:15–00:30 | Reproducible writing | Project map |
| 00:30–00:50 | Markdown | Structured manuscript |
| 0:50–01:05 | Break | |
| 01:05–01:35 | Computation | Live figure, table, and inline result |
| 01:35–02:00 | Research publishing | HTML, PDF, and journal-format demo |

## How to use this book

Keep the book open beside your editor. Green **Try it** boxes are the main
hands-on path. Yellow **Checkpoint** boxes describe what should work before the
room moves on. Purple **Discussion** boxes are brief pauses for interpretation.
Blue **If you finish early** boxes are optional and can be skipped without
affecting later exercises.

The main path assumes R. A compact [Python/Jupyter
translation](appendices/python.qmd) is provided for later use.
